clue.text: Famous European family retreating in food resort hotel

indicators.note: going backwards, so the whole string of pieces is read in reverse order

parts.note: grub is slang for food
a spa is a health resort
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A grand dynasty pulling back to a hotel at a resort known for its food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' reverses the whole string of pieces, not just the last one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Habsburgs, sometimes spelt this way, were the ruling dynasty of Austria and the Holy Roman Empire.

clue.text: Conditions for favourable growth? It means one shouldn't have cold feet

definitions.meaning: an environment that encourages rapid growth of something

definitions.text: It means one shouldn't have cold feet
definitions.meaning: read literally, a ... keeps a sleeper's feet warm

explanation.surface: Talk of gardening conditions, then a reassurance against cold feet in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotbed is a heated bed of soil for raising plants, and figuratively any place where something flourishes.

clue.text: Grim-faced worker penning book — something to earn fast buck?

parts.note: po-faced means grim or disapproving, giving the first two letters

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the book letter goes inside

parts.note: a toiler is a hard worker

explanation.surface: A dour labourer writes a book purely to make quick money.
explanation.definitionFit: A potboiler is a hastily written work produced chiefly for income, to keep the pot boiling.

clue.text: Wild animal mostly existing in captivity to make money

indicators.note: one piece is held captive inside the animal

parts.note: a boar is a wild pig

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: live means existing, alive

explanation.surface: A wild beast kept caged so that someone can profit from it.
explanation.definitionFit: The bolívar is the currency of Venezuela, named after Simón Bolívar.

clue.text: Part of machine soldiers set up on pile of rocks

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: OR, Other Ranks, are soldiers who are not officers
a tor is a rocky outcrop on a hill

explanation.surface: Troops erect a mechanical part on top of a rocky hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating component of a machine such as a motor or turbine.

clue.text: State offers something worth having — it's right to join in

indicators.note: the letter for right comes in to join the other word, so it goes inside it

parts.note: an asset is a valuable thing to possess

explanation.surface: Someone declares that an offer is valuable and that it is fair to take part.
explanation.definitionFit: To state something firmly is to declare it, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Disfigured king, frightened to go about

indicators.note: the frightened word goes around the king letter, enclosing it

parts.note: scared means frightened
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A scarred king too frightened to venture out.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarred means marked by scars, so damaged in appearance.

clue.text: Chosen group among the literati

indicators.note: among says the answer lies within the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A select circle within the literary set.
explanation.definitionFit: An elite is a select group regarded as the best, from French for chosen.

clue.text: Worker in the office for a while — smart, not initially alluring

parts.words: Worker in the office for a while
parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to smart is to sting

explanation.surface: A temporary office worker, smartly turned out, who is rather attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempting means attractive and enticing, much the same as alluring.

clue.text: Conservative was first to hold seat and was overcome?

indicators.note: the Conservative-plus-led string holds the seat word inside it

parts.note: led means was in front, came first
the rump is the buttocks, the part one sits on

explanation.surface: A Tory who led the race to win a seat but then lost heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seat' is the backside, not a parliamentary seat.
explanation.definitionFit: To crumple is to collapse or give way, as someone overwhelmed does.

clue.text: Horrible attritional aims in dictatorship?

indicators.note: horrible suggests the letters of the two words are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A dictatorship with horrible aims of wearing down its people.
explanation.definitionFit: Totalitarianism is a system of absolute centralised state control, the defining feature of a dictatorship; the question mark flags definition by example.

clue.text: It's an arm, not the head, that adapts slowly

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is left off here

parts.note: a revolver is a firearm, so an arm

explanation.surface: A limb that, minus its head, slowly changes shape — like some sci-fi creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an arm' is a weapon, not a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that evolves changes gradually over time, so it is one that adapts slowly.

clue.text: Ornament in part of south London by road junction

parts.note: Morden is a district at the southern end of the Northern line in London
a T-junction is where one road meets another at right angles

explanation.surface: A decorative feature found near a crossroads in a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: MORDEN is a south London suburb, the end of the Northern Underground line.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a mordent is a trill-like ornament: a quick alternation with the note below or above.

clue.text: Man bound by special call connected with the priesthood?

indicators.note: one piece is held inside the other, as if tied up by it
special suggests the letters of the word call are given an unusual arrangement

parts.note: Eric is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man tied to a special vocation, the calling of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' rearranges the fodder to CLAL; the man's name sits inside it. The question mark admits the definition is a loose fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Clerical means relating to the clergy, the body of ordained priests.

clue.text: Circle is not put in a difficult situation

definitions.meaning: a circle has no angles, so it is not this

explanation.surface: A circle, it seems, is not someone put in a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cornered means trapped, as in a corner; literally the word also means having corners, which a circle lacks.

clue.text: Mother performing as a legendary friend

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
on, as in on stage, means performing

explanation.surface: Mum, on stage, plays the part of a famous friend from legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Damon and Pythias are the Greek legend's model of loyal friendship, Damon offering his life as surety for Pythias.

clue.text: What could produce ailment? No hormone

indicators.note: the answer's letters, rearranged, produce the words that follow, so they are anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A worried question whether something causes illness, answered no — it's a natural hormone.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram runs backwards: the answer rearranged produces AILMENT + NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Melatonin is the hormone secreted by the pineal gland that regulates sleep cycles.

clue.text: A hundred cushions in East End churches? They are hung up in the vestry

definitions.text: They are hung up in the vestry

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: Cockney speech in London's East End drops the initial H

parts.note: hassocks are kneeling cushions

explanation.surface: A hundred kneeling cushions in the churches of East London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in East End' drops H from HASSOCKS, the way Cockneys drop their aitches.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassocks are clergy's long robes, kept on pegs in the vestry, the room where clergy robe.

clue.text: One's crossing river to see lots of territory?

indicators.note: the river letter goes across, so it sits inside the other word

parts.note: one is ace, and with the apostrophe s it reads as ace's

explanation.surface: Someone fords a river to look over a vast expanse of land.
explanation.definitionFit: Acres are units of land area, and in the plural an informal way of saying a great deal of ground.

clue.text: Dull sort of editor failed to get to grips with English

parts.note: a sub is a subeditor

indicators.note: the failed word grips the letter for English inside it

parts.note: a dud is something that failed

explanation.surface: A dreary subeditor who never got to grips with the English language.
explanation.definitionFit: Subdued means muted or low-key, so lacking brightness or liveliness.

clue.text: Clear one bad clue may get this!

definitions.text: Clear one bad clue may get this!

parts.note: to rid a place is to clear it
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of the word clue are scrambled

explanation.surface: A setter's warning that a poor clue invites scorn from solvers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' turns CLUE into CULE. The whole clue is also the definition: a bad clue may get mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridicule is mockery or derision, exactly what solvers heap on a poorly made clue.

clue.text: Like a rogue in the money, did wrong, getting imprisoned

indicators.note: the mixed-up letters are locked up inside the money word

parts.note: cash is money

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters of did are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rogue in the money who did wrong and got locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: A cad is an ungentlemanly rogue, so caddish means behaving like a scoundrel.

clue.text: Petition park to rear type of cactus

indicators.note: in a down clue, rearing means rising up, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: to sue is to petition or appeal
a rec is a recreation ground, a park

explanation.surface: An appeal to the park to grow a certain cactus.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereus is a genus of columnar cacti, including the night-blooming cereus.

clue.text: Weird globules, finally fading away — able to break down in water?

definitions.text: able to break down in water?

indicators.note: weird suggests the letters are rearranged into something strange
away tells us the picked letter is removed from the mix
finally points to the last letter of the word fading

explanation.surface: Strange little globules, finally fading away, as if dissolving in water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally fading' is G; 'away' takes it out of GLOBULES, and 'Weird' shuffles what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A soluble substance dissolves, and water is the usual solvent in mind.

clue.text: Dance to get leg under or leg over?

parts.note: a leg is a limb
O is the abbreviation for over in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A dance where you have to get a leg under a bar — or over it?
explanation.walkthrough: In the limbo dancers bend backwards to pass under a low bar; 'or' links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The limbo is a West Indian dance in which dancers lean back to pass beneath a lowering bar.

clue.text: Short communication about a daughter being not the sort you want?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the letters go around the inserted pair
short means cut off before the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a letter is a written communication

explanation.surface: A brief note about one's daughter suggesting she isn't the kind of girl you'd hope for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' is British slang for a woman, here an undesirable one.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladette is a young woman given to boisterous, loutish behaviour, arguably not a desirable sort of girl.

clue.text: Composer that's unknown's turning up in reading material

indicators.note: the turned piece sits inside the reading-material word

parts.note: lit is short for literature

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means read from bottom to top, so reversed

parts.note: Z is an algebraic unknown, plus the possessive s

explanation.surface: A composer's name turning up, unknown, in some book.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian Romantic composer and piano virtuoso.

clue.text: Awkwardly cope with music centre that features modern electronics

indicators.note: awkwardly suggests the letters are clumsily rearranged

explanation.surface: Struggling to cope with a hi-fi music centre full of newfangled electronics.
explanation.walkthrough: A music centre is an all-in-one home stereo system.
explanation.definitionFit: Computer science is the field of study built around computing hardware and software, which relies on modern electronics.

clue.text: Poor-quality pitch — what's unusual in that?

indicators.note: the unusual word goes inside the pitch word

parts.note: to shy is to throw or pitch something
odd means unusual

explanation.surface: A dodgy playing surface, with something odd about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' looks like a sports field but is a throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy goods are badly made or of inferior quality.

clue.text: Pieces of artwork Greek character inscribed in gents naughtily

indicators.note: the letter is written inside the other piece
naughtily suggests the letters of gents are rearranged mischievously

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Graffiti in Greek scrawled on the walls of a men's lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughtily' shuffles the fodder to ETNGS. 'Gents' is the British word for a men's public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Etchings are prints made from designs bitten into metal plates with acid, a kind of artwork.
